citations.quote: Study CS3B was a 13-month, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-procedure controlled trial in patients with infantile-onset SMA.
This is a Phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, sham-procedure-controlled study of ISIS 396443 administered intrathecally over 13 months to patients with infantile-onset SMA.

design.text: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-procedure controlled trial; approximately 111 subjects were to be randomized 2:1 to a scaled-equivalent 12 mg dose of nusinersen intrathecally or a sham procedure

citations.quote: This is a Phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, sham-procedure-controlled study of ISIS 396443 administered intrathecally over 13 months to patients with infantile-onset SMA. Approximately 111 subjects were to be randomized 2:1 to receive a scaled equivalent 12 mg dose ISIS 396443 or undergo a sham procedure as control, respectively.

population.text: Patients with infantile-onset SMA who have 2 copies of the SMN2 gene; males and females ≤ 7 months (210 days) of age at screening

citations.quote: This application includes data from an interim analysis of a double-blind, sham-procedure controlled trial in infantile-onset SMA patients who have 2 copies of the SMN2 gene (Study CS3B).
In the Controlled Study CS3B, subjects were males and females \leq 7 months (210 days) of age at screening.

endpoint.text: Proportion of motor milestone responders (based on Section 2 of the Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination)

citations.quote: 1. Proportion of motor milestone responders.
The Interim Efficacy Data seems to support the efficacy of ISIS 396443 (Nusinersen) in terms of the primary endpoint, Motor Milestone Responder Rate.

Motor milestones were to be determined during screening (the baseline assessment) and on Days 64, 183, 302, and 394 using Section 2 of the Hammersmith Infant Neurological Examination (HINE) which is comprised of eight tests: head control, sitting, voluntary grasp, ability to kick in supine position, rolling, crawling, standing, and walking (see Table 2).

n.text: 121 subjects in the ITT population received at least 1 dose (nusinersen n=80, sham control n=41) as of the June 15, 2016 interim analysis

citations.quote: As of the June 15, 2016 data cut-off for the interim analysis, a total of 121 subjects received at least 1 dose of study treatment (ISIS 396443 (n= 80) or sham procedure control (n= 41)) and were included in the ITT population.

result.text: A statistically significantly greater proportion achieved a motor milestone response in the nusinersen group (21; 41%) versus sham control (0; 0%), p < 0.0001

citations.quote: A statistically significantly greater proportion of subjects achieved a motor milestone response in the ISIS 396443 group (21; 41%) compared to the sham control group (0; 0%) (p < 0.0001).

indication.text: SPINRAZA is indicated for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in pediatric and adult patients

citations.quote: SPINRAZA is indicated for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in pediatric and adult patients.

target_moa.text: Nusinersen is a survival motor neuron-2 (SMN2)-directed antisense oligonucleotide that binds a sequence in the intron downstream of exon 7 of the SMN2 transcript, increasing exon 7 inclusion in SMN2 mRNA and production of full-length SMN protein

citations.quote: SPINRAZA is a survival motor neuron-2 (SMN2)-directed antisense oligonucleotide indicated for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in pediatric and adult patients (1)
Nusinersen binds to a specific sequence in the intron downstream of exon 7 of the *SMN2* transcript.
SPINRAZA was shown to increase exon 7 inclusion in *SMN2* messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) transcripts and production of full-length SMN protein.

modality.text: Oligonucleotide (18-mer antisense oligonucleotide with phosphorothioate backbone)

citations.quote: This application under review is for nusinersen (ISIS 396443), an 18-mer antisense oligonucleotide formulated as a solution for intrathecal administration for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥20% and ≥5% more than control) were lower respiratory infection (43% vs 29%), upper respiratory infection (39% vs 34%), and constipation (30% vs 22%); serious atelectasis was more frequent (14% vs 5%). Warnings include thrombocytopenia/coagulation abnormalities and renal toxicity.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions that occurred in at least 20% of SPINRAZA-treated patients and occurred at least 5% more frequently than in control patients were lower respiratory infection, upper respiratory infection, and constipation (6.1)

Lower respiratory infection2	43	29

Serious adverse reactions of atelectasis were more frequent in SPINRAZA-treated patients (14%) than in control patients (5%).
Coagulation abnormalities and thrombocytopenia, including acute severe thrombocytopenia, have been observed after administration of some antisense oligonucleotides.
Renal toxicity, including potentially fatal glomerulonephritis, has been observed after administration of some antisense oligonucleotides.

description.text: Updated labeling with efficacy/safety data from controlled trials in infantile-onset and later-onset SMA and presymptomatic SMA, not a new indication.

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to the labeling that were based on results from controlled clinical trials in infantile-onset spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and in later-onset SMA, as well as interim results from an open-label study in presymptomatic SMA. The revisions include changes to section 5 (Warnings and Precautions), section 6 (Adverse Reactions), section 12.2 (Pharmacodynamics), and section 14 (Clinical Studies) of the prescribing information (PI). In addition, this supplement provides for an update to section 2 (Dosage and Administration) to include language that the use of an external filter is not required, and the correction of the molecular structure of nusinersen in section 11 (Description) of the PI.

description.text: Updated labeling with interim results from the open-label study in patients with presymptomatic spinal muscular atrophy (SMA)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to labeling, to include updated interim results from the open-label study of patients with presymptomatic spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). The revisions include the following changes to the Spinraza prescribing information (PI):

description.text: Added a higher dosing regimen with two new strength presentations (28 mg/5 mL and 50 mg/5 mL)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for revisions throughout the Prescribing Information (PI) regarding a completed clinical study [Study 4 (NCT04089566)], which provides an additional higher dosing regimen. Two corresponding additional strength presentations [28 mg/5 mL (5.6 mg/mL) and 50 mg/5 mL (10 mg/mL)] are included for administration of the new dosing regimen. This sNDA also includes revisions to the Pediatric Use subsection (8.4) of the PI to include results from a combined 6- and 13-week toxicity study in juvenile monkeys.
